narrative:
The model predicted a 60% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability exceeded the school's acceptance threshold, your law school application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were your undergraduate GPA, your LSAT score, and your academic performance in the third year of law school. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.20 was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure; it sits well below the 3.23 average of students who were accepted. Your LSAT score of 31 was the second most important factor and also increased the likelihood of failure, falling noticeably short of the 37.18 average among accepted applicants. These two academic measures together created the bulk of the concern.

Your third-year law school ranking provided a modest counter-balance, slightly lowering the predicted risk of failure, but it was not enough to offset the earlier signals. Other details such as your lower-middle family income, full-time study plans, gender, and race played no role in the decision.

To improve your chances in a future application, focus on raising your LSAT score and strengthening your academic record where possible. Retaking the LSAT after targeted preparation is likely the highest-impact step you can take right now.
